first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and simplification directly addresses the shared funnel constraint with prior evidence of durable early-adoption improvement. Verify the onboarding evidence and the pricing evidence because targeted discounting is highly consequential under competitive pressure but needs confirmation on sustainable qualified-revenue effects.

mid.rationale: Run a standard onboarding-simplification experiment. It directly addresses the 4% completion decline and likely contributes to the 6% activation decline; its verified prior result improved completion (+13%), time-to-value (-2.1 days), and 30-day retention (+3%). Promotional pricing is ruled out for the sustainable-revenue objective because its verified cohort had 30-day retention fall 12%. Flag residual downstream risk because the onboarding evidence establishes retention only through 30 days, not full long-term qualified-revenue durability.

final2.rationale: Keep the cycle focused on onboarding simplification: it is the strongest verified sustainable-growth lever available, directly addresses declining completion and activation, and previously improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. Do not respond with broad promotional pricing: the verified discount experiment raised qualified revenue short term but reduced 30-day retention by 12%, conflicting with the long-term objective. The deeper competitor cut raises immediate SMB churn risk, but its incremental impact and whether a narrower non-discount response could mitigate it are unverified; flag this for next-cycle measurement.
